attributes.board_name: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation – Occupational Therapy Board

rules.accepted_credit_types: Approved-sponsor programs (incl. distance learning); college courses (15 hours per semester hour, 10 per quarter hour, no cap). Other activities with caps per period: independent study max 4; study groups max 12; mentorship max 8; fieldwork educator 1 h per week per student max 12; OTD capstone mentor max 14; writing (book 18, chapter/article/editing 12, non-professional article 6); presenting incl. prep max 12; research max 12; grants max 12; board/committee work 2 per appointment max 8; volunteer service 2 per 5 h max 12; specialty certification 12 each; AOTA residency/fellowship 1 per 2 h max 24. No credit for courses taken in Illinois from unapproved sponsors.
rules.new_licensee_rule: Not required for the first renewal after the license is issued.
rules.audit_note: Certify full compliance on the renewal application; the Division may request evidence, so keep proof. Waivers for military service or extreme hardship by request with the renewal.

topics.who: Implicit bias awareness training (20 ILCS 2105/2105-15.7); from July 1, 2026, licensees providing maternal health care need a version covering maternal health risks

Only licensees with direct patient interaction with adults aged 26+ (20 ILCS 2105/2105-365). Rule says each renewal period; IDFPR's CE page says before the first CE renewal on/after Jan 1, 2025, then every 6 years
Renewals on or after Jan 1, 2025: before the first renewal requiring CE, then once every 6 years; counts toward the 24

rules.notes: 24 contact hours = 12 units of Continued Competency Activities (2 contact hours = 1 unit); 1 contact hour = 50 minutes, half-hour increments after the first hour. Prerenewal period = 24 months before December 31 of the renewal year; all OT and OTA licenses expire December 31 of odd-numbered years. Rule amended effective April 5, 2024.
